quote: Believe that life is worth living, and your belief will help create the fact.
source: William James, Is Life Worth Living?, in The Will to Believe, final paragraph (1897)
note: Not the closing sentence. It stands in the final paragraph, after “These, then, are my last words to you: Be not afraid of life”, and the essay closes with the Henry IV and Crillon anecdote. James italicises “is”, which the card cannot show.

evidence.where: Project Gutenberg #26659, The Will to Believe and Other Essays in Popular Philosophy (Longmans, Green, 1897), plain text, lines 2218 to 2227
evidence.edition: The Will to Believe and Other Essays in Popular Philosophy, Longmans, Green, 1897
evidence.locator: Is Life Worth Living?, final paragraph

reason: The words are James’s exactly, but the locator was wrong: the sentence opens the final paragraph rather than ending the essay, and the original emphasises “is”.
